summary: classes_catalog and classes_search's underlying endpoint (/api/v2/ride/archived) always returns ride_types/class_types sidecar vocabulary arrays (234 items each, static catalog data unrelated to the query, already fully available via classes_filters' class_type_id/ride_type_id filter entries) alongside the real "data" results. makeAPIHandlerStripFields (internal/mcp/tools.go) strips named top-level object keys from a successful response before it reaches bound.go's trimming logic; both classes_catalog and classes_search pass rideArchivedRedundantFields (=["ride_types","class_types"]) to it. This is deliberately narrower than teaching bound.go's shared single-array-field trimmer to handle multi-array envelopes generically -- a scoped, endpoint-specific fix carries far less risk than touching logic every typed tool depends on. Any future regen must keep classes_catalog/classes_search wired through makeAPIHandlerStripFields (not the plain makeAPIHandler) with this field list; if Peloton's real API response shape for /api/v2/ride/archived changes to drop or rename these fields, this patch degrades to a safe no-op (stripTopLevelFields never errors on an absent key) rather than breaking.
reason: SIGNIFICANT #6 from a live post-fix verification sweep (structured findings report against the user's real account): responses from these two tools large enough to need MCP result-budget trimming have three array fields (data, ride_types, class_types), which defeats bound.go's boundedSingleArrayObject/boundedSingleArrayPageObject heuristic (it can only identify "the" list field when exactly one array is present) -- so instead of a proper bounded item list, the tool returned an unbounded raw JSON preview, which is both less useful to an agent and does not reliably surface the actual data field if ride_types/class_types happen to serialize first. Confirmed live against the real API that ride_types/class_types are pure static vocabulary duplicating classes_filters' class_type_id/ride_type_id filter entries (same id/display_name pairs), so stripping them loses no information reachable elsewhere. User was asked to choose between (a) strip in the response builder, (b) generalize the shared trimmer, (c) both, and (d) leave typed-tool argument passthrough (SIGNIFICANT #3/#5, a related but separate finding) as-is with just documentation added -- chose (a) conditioned on it not being a breaking change for other MCP consumers, and (d) for the passthrough question. Breaking-change risk assessed as effectively nil: this fix branch/PR has not been published yet (no external consumer of this specific behavior exists), the fields are read-only static catalog noise rather than a documented API contract, and the same data remains reachable via classes_filters for any caller that does depend on it.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck all green. New tests: TestMCPToolResultTextMultiArrayEnvelopeFallsBackToRawPreview reproduces the underlying bound.go limitation directly; TestStripTopLevelFieldsRemovesRedundantCatalogVocabulary confirms stripping fixes the same fixture end-to-end (proper bounded envelope with correct total_count/returned_count instead of a raw preview); TestStripTopLevelFieldsIsNoOpWhenFieldsAbsentOrNotAnObject guards the helper's safety contract. Live-verified against the user's real account: a throwaway test invoked the actual registered classes_catalog tool handler end-to-end and confirmed ride_types/class_types are absent from the real response while every other field (data, count, page, browse_categories, fitness_disciplines, instructors, etc.) passes through unchanged.
